title: rec-c2.1-tripwire-evidence
summary: Tripwire firings become durable ExecutionLog evidence. C2.1.1 adds ExecutionKind::TripwireFired (appended last; Raw=0/GapMarker=1 pinned) and TripwireFiredEvidence { tripwire_id, source_seq: EventSeq, source_event_id, condition, label, source_timestamp_ns, source_thread_id }, plus the NewExecutionRecord.kind field the backends previously hardcoded to Raw. C2.1.2 inverts dual_push: append first, publish only on success (no observation without acceptance). C2.1.3 derives firings from an accepted Raw record with the recursion barrier enforced by ExecutionKind. C2.1.4-7 (observe-from-log with an independent consumer cursor, derived fire_count, honest retained_until_session_end, fired_buffer removal, restart UAT) are NOT done: observe is synchronous and cannot reach the active session id behind a tokio Mutex; see tasks.md.

no_action: FIND-C2.1-03 (derivation has no production caller; scoped to REC-C2.2)

findings_detail.FIND-C2.1-01: NewExecutionRecord had no `kind` field: both backends hardcoded `kind: ExecutionKind::Raw`, so any non-raw record was silently stored as Raw. Found while making the derivation tests pass; fixed by adding the field and honouring it in the in-memory and segmented backends.
findings_detail.FIND-C2.1-02: scripts/check_legacy_evb.py miscounted a token inside a `"...\`-continued string as production code (it appeared in a message literal). The ratchet flagged it as a new use; strip_noise now carries string state across lines, and the inventory legitimately shrank 37 -> 36.
